title: Charles XII to the Rådet and his envoys, Bender, 26 April 1710 (catalogue 599): two copies in a Swedish homophonic nomenclator, key rebuilt by crib

documents.shelfmark: Niedersächsisches Landesarchiv, Abt. Stade, Rep. 5a Nr. 670 (old shelfmark Fach 76 Nr. 38), fols. 83–85; file “Diverse chiffrierte Schreiben von und an Generalgouverneur Baron Nils Gyllenstierna”, 1700–1711
documents.route: Bender -> Stockholm (Rådet); London and The Hague (envoys); copies to Stade

plaintext.source: No key or decipherment with the copies; the two copies encipher partly different words and check each other.

transcription.notes: Doubtful numbers checked blind on the image by Brice Dudout.

system.summary: homophonic Swedish nomenclator of about 1,100 numbers in alphabetical order: letters (31–98, two series), syllables (99–182), numbers (183–211), endings (212–304), words and names (310–1102); powers written as sigla in clear: B.B. = Denmark, LL = England, ddd = Holland

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 599 open; no key in the file; web search 27 Oct 2026.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Ciphered troop list (fols. 73, 82) aligned with its clear draft (fol. 74); totals and officers' names fixed the first values, then the alphabetical structure of the table.
Key frozen, applied to pages never opened before: fol. 100 (German, 93% of words recognised) and fols. 78v-79r (96%); permuted and shuffled control keys at most 77-80%.
Both copies of the 26 April 1710 letter read and compared; 639 of 640 groups read.
Doubtful numbers checked blind on the image by Brice Dudout; the two copies cross-check (same words, sometimes clear in one copy and cipher in the other).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from a ciphered troop list in the same file whose clear draft survives, then frozen and validated on unseen letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 639 of 640 cipher groups read; six probable readings marked on the write-up.

human_check.passage: doubtful numbers of the two copies

texts.label: Charles XII, Bender, 26 April 1710: copies for the envoys (fol. 85) and for the Rådet (fols. 83-84)
texts.summary: A refugee at Bender, on Ottoman soil, since Poltava, Charles XII learns of the rout of the Danish army at Helsingborg. In a chancery letter whose sensitive passages are in cipher, he declares himself ready to make peace with Denmark under the mediation of England and the United Provinces, and gives the Council a “free hand” to negotiate and to conclude an armistice, “even for a whole year”. Two ciphered copies, received by the Swedish government of Bremen-Verden, are kept at Stade.
